purpose: Live Power Stack thematic radar; dynamic ranking by freshness/materiality and current market significance. Theme rank changes research priority, not company fundamental scores.

environment.label: Capital scarcity + AI funding selectivity + agentic dispersion + crude relief
environment.summary: Crude and long-end relief still support selective AI/duration risk-on, but the deeper Sep 23 research shows a sharper split between AI equity/adoption momentum and the financing layer. Project-finance loans/bonds, delayed IPOs and sponsor guarantees raise the cost-of-capital hurdle, while financials face both curve pressure and a new agentic-disintermediation question. Broad risk-on remains incomplete.

whatIsNewNow: AI project finance is repricing even while AI equities/adoption remain strong: Project Jupiter debt stress, weaker Hyperion project bonds and delayed SB Energy/Holtec IPO plans make funding quality a first-order signal.

Sponsor support now matters explicitly: Nvidia's disclosed residual-value/credit support for initial SB Energy/OpenAI capacity shows that guarantees can lower funding costs without eliminating counterparty, execution or concentration risk.
The funding window is selective rather than closed: Nscale's continued IPO process is a counterexample to a blanket 'AI capital markets are shut' thesis.
Financial weakness now has two competing mechanisms to test: flatter-curve/NIM pressure and agentic-AI disintermediation of wealth, insurance and consumer-financial interfaces.
Breadth is not one signal: weak 52-week highs/lows can coexist with positive same-session advance/decline and stronger semiconductor leadership.
WTI relief remains faster than proof of refined-product normalization; diesel-export policy risk, ULSD/cracks, freight and refinery utilization remain separate checks.
Front/belly rates staying firm while oil falls would point increasingly toward demand/real-rate/issuance pressure rather than energy inflation alone.
whatMattersMostToMarketsNow: AI credit supply / project-finance cost of capital
Funded/contracted AI demand vs financing-dependent capacity
Agentic AI disruption vs flatter-curve bank pressure
Breadth decomposition: cap-weight, equal-weight, semis, banks and new highs/lows

themes.name: Capital Scarcity / AI Credit + Project-Finance Dispersion
themes.whyNow: AI equities and adoption remain strong while the financing layer reprices: Project Jupiter loans trade at stressed discounts, Hyperion project bonds have weakened, SB Energy/Holtec delayed IPO plans and large sponsor guarantees expose execution, concentration and cost-of-capital risk. This is capital selectivity, not yet a shutdown of AI funding.
themes.marketTransmission: project finance, corporate spreads, sponsor guarantees, IPO valuation, capex hurdle rates, equity multiples
themes.confirmation: AI/project debt stays wider or new issuance needs concessions while equity leadership and contracted physical orders persist
themes.invalidation: project debt normalizes, IPOs clear cleanly at targeted valuations and FCF/ROIC improves without rising sponsor support
themes.nextTest: Project Jupiter/Hyperion marks, SB Energy/Nscale pricing, new hyperscaler issuance, guarantees and credit breadth
themes.watchlistHoldingAction: Favor existing cash-generative and contracted physical demand; penalize pre-operating, concentrated or guarantee-dependent capacity.

themes.name: AI Infrastructure Demand + Grid Access / Permitting
themes.whyNow: AI demand remains strong, but realizable capacity must clear financing, customer concentration, guarantees, power, permitting, water and construction tests. Nscale's continued IPO process argues against a blanket funding-collapse call, while delayed SB Energy/Holtec offerings show investors are demanding better terms for pre-operating risk.
themes.marketTransmission: data-centre finance, utilities, generation, permitting, supplier backlog, water/cooling
themes.confirmation: signed customers plus diversified counterparties, permits/interconnection/self-supply, funded construction and FCF conversion
themes.invalidation: broad cancellations or rapid grid-capacity normalization
themes.nextTest: customer concentration, sponsor guarantees, deposits, IPO/project-finance terms, grid approvals and energized MW
themes.watchlistHoldingAction: Prefer operating assets and suppliers with funded backlogs; heavily discount speculative MW and long-dated single-tenant economics.

themes.name: Power / Grid / Electrical Bottlenecks + Self-Supply
themes.whyNow: Amazon/Generac validates signed backup-generation demand while grid/permitting constraints keep generation, transformers, switchgear and cables scarce.
themes.marketTransmission: generation, backup power, transformers, switchgear, cables, utility capex
themes.confirmation: signed orders, funded projects, permits/interconnection and energized MW
themes.nextTest: supplier orders, customer deposits and YTL contracted load
themes.watchlistHoldingAction: YTLPOWR hold; GNRC priority research/no chase; ETN/PWR quality with valuation discipline.

themes.name: Financial-System Transmission / Banks + Agentic Disintermediation
themes.whyNow: Nasdaq/AI is strong while banks and wealth intermediaries lag. The weakness may reflect both a flatter curve and a new agentic-AI threat to wealth, insurance and consumer-financial interfaces; private-credit redemption pressure remains a separate credit-transmission warning.
themes.marketTransmission: yield curve, NIM, wealth/insurance distribution, lending appetite, private-credit liquidity, small caps, cyclicals
themes.confirmation: wealth/intermediary names underperform comparable rate-sensitive lenders while bank/credit breadth remains weak
themes.invalidation: curve steepens constructively, bank relative strength recovers and wealth/intermediary underperformance disappears as agent products mature
themes.nextTest: SCHW/AMP/RJF vs JPM/BAC/C/KRE, 2s10s, NIM sensitivity, credit spreads and private-credit redemptions
themes.watchlistHoldingAction: Use financials as a risk-on confirmation gate; do not attribute weakness to AI alone until relative-performance and rate controls support it.

themes.name: Agentic AI / Inference + Intermediary Disruption
themes.whyNow: Agentic/inference adoption is broadening the AI trade beyond frontier training while creating potential losers among wealth, insurance, subscriptions and other consumer intermediaries. The market is beginning to price both beneficiary and disruption baskets.
themes.marketTransmission: software/inference demand, commerce interfaces, wealth/insurance distribution, payments, consumer intermediaries
themes.confirmation: agent adoption/monetization improves while intermediary relative weakness persists beyond rate-driven explanations
themes.invalidation: agent usage fails to monetize or financial-intermediary weakness fully reverses with curve normalization
themes.nextTest: META agent engagement/monetization, SCHW/AMP/RJF relative performance, enterprise agent bookings and inference demand
themes.watchlistHoldingAction: Research beneficiaries and disrupted intermediaries separately; no blanket long-AI/short-financials trade.

themes.name: AI Security / Independent Model Evaluation
themes.whyNow: Palo Alto launched a globally sold annual-subscription service using frontier models for continuous vulnerability testing, moving AI-security demand from hypothesis toward monetizable product evidence.
themes.marketTransmission: cyber budgets, AI governance, recurring security subscriptions, consulting/evaluation spend
themes.invalidation: enterprise spend remains experimental or commoditized
themes.nextTest: PANW/CRWD bookings, renewal economics and regulatory mandates
themes.watchlistHoldingAction: Raise research priority; selective pullbacks only, no blanket SaaS upgrade.

themes.name: Critical Minerals / Copper / Tungsten + Recycling
themes.whyNow: Strategic shortages remain active and Nth Cycle's $1B Glencore offtake adds commercial proof that recycling/refining can become a differentiated supply-security layer.
themes.marketTransmission: AI hardware, grid capex, cables, defense, industrial policy, recycling/refining
themes.confirmation: persistent physical premiums/shortages plus funded offtakes/refining capacity
themes.nextTest: physical inventories/premiums, US-China policy and recycling economics
themes.watchlistHoldingAction: FCX preferred-zone research; investigate cash-generative refiners/recyclers; avoid speculative pre-revenue miners.

themes.name: Middle East Refined Products + Shipping
themes.directionOfTravel: crude weakening fast; products still unconfirmed
themes.whyNow: WTI below $90 and Saudi bypass restoration show a fast crude-premium unwind, but structural diesel/jet tightness and same-session crack behavior still need confirmation. The crude/products divergence now matters more than outright oil direction.
themes.marketTransmission: diesel, freight, tanker rates, inflation, farm/consumer margins
themes.confirmation: ULSD/jet cracks and freight remain elevated despite WTI/Brent weakness
themes.invalidation: product inventories rebuild, cracks/freight normalize and route capacity recovers
themes.nextTest: ULSD/3-2-1, EIA distillates/gasoline, refinery utilization, tanker rates and Yanbu throughput
themes.watchlistHoldingAction: Prefer integrated/refining quality over pure upstream war beta; no headline chase.

themes.name: US LNG Rerouting + Market Access
themes.whyNow: Structural diversification remains intact, but Hormuz reopening hopes reduce near-term scarcity urgency. LNG at $272.96 remains in the original excellent/preferred area.
themes.marketTransmission: US gas demand, LNG contracting, Asian/European gas prices
themes.confirmation: new SPAs, high utilization and market-access improvement
themes.invalidation: weak contracting plus normalized Gulf supply
themes.nextTest: new SPAs, China access and Gulf normalization
themes.watchlistHoldingAction: LNG remains high-quality entry research, but no geopolitical chase.

themes.name: Agriculture / Fertilizer / Food Affordability
themes.whyNow: El Nino food-risk remains live while energy/fertilizer affordability is improving unevenly. Demand elasticity remains segmented by input type.
themes.marketTransmission: food inflation, farm margins, input volumes, machinery capex
themes.confirmation: crop/input ratios improve and export demand strengthens
themes.invalidation: farm margins deteriorate enough to cut core inputs
themes.nextTest: crop margins, nitrogen/phosphate/potash prices, diesel and weather
themes.watchlistHoldingAction: CTVA/BG first; CF/NTR selective; VMI later; AGCO second-stage only.

themes.name: Uranium / Nuclear Fuel + Buildout
themes.whyNow: Fuel-cycle localization and long-duration power remain strategic, but no fresh Sep 22 catalyst outranks credit/grid/security.
themes.marketTransmission: uranium contracting, enrichment, reactor supply chain
themes.watchlistHoldingAction: CCJ remains preferred quality research; maintain valuation discipline.

themes.name: AI Memory / HBM Scarcity
themes.whyNow: Semiconductor leadership remains strong and the memory/HBM scarcity thesis is intact. Creator-reported bearish MU positioning is retained only as challenger evidence requiring filing/valuation/supply verification.
themes.marketTransmission: HBM/DRAM pricing, server BOM, semiconductor margins
themes.confirmation: HBM contracts and memory pricing remain firm
themes.invalidation: inventory correction or rapid supply response
themes.nextTest: HBM/DRAM pricing, contracts, inventories/capacity and independently verified bearish positioning
themes.watchlistHoldingAction: MU remains preferred listed US expression; no vertical chase and no creator-driven downgrade.

themes.name: Robotics / Automation Commercialization
themes.whyNow: IFR reports only ~7,000 humanoids sold globally in 2025 versus hundreds of thousands of conventional industrial/service robots; Toyota's planned factory-automation spend reinforces near-term commercial priority for fixed automation.
themes.marketTransmission: factory automation, machine vision, motion control, robotics capex
themes.confirmation: external recurring revenue and measurable productivity ROI
themes.nextTest: RoboTechnik HK pricing and Toyota supplier beneficiaries

themes.name: Gold / Silver / Miners
themes.whyNow: Long yields and oil have eased, but DXY remains firm under a hawkish Fed. Miners are worth relative-strength investigation, not promotion, until dollar/real-yield pressure weakens.
themes.invalidation: real yields/dollar surge with weaker physical/ETF demand
themes.nextTest: DXY, 5Y/10Y real yields, GDX/GLD and central-bank/ETF flows
themes.watchlistHoldingAction: Investigate miner relative strength; no tactical upgrade while DXY remains firm.

themes.name: ESS Demand vs Battery Manufacturing Overcapacity
themes.whyNow: Critical-mineral recycling/offtake is improving, but China battery-manufacturing overcapacity remains a warning against generic cell/lithium exposure.
themes.marketTransmission: storage integrators, cells, lithium pricing, utility capex
themes.nextTest: China approvals, deployments, recycling economics and margins
themes.watchlistHoldingAction: Favor storage cash conversion; generic lithium remains background/dormant.
